correctness.rationale: The factorization S_r(p^a)=p^(a-1)(p-r) for p>r shows that every positive block in a preimage of ell^t is an ell-power. A nonspecial source prime therefore has exponent one and equals r+ell^j. The only repeated source prime is ell=r+1, where its exponent contributes a-1. The resulting subset-sum bijection proves both coefficient formulas and all stated corollaries. The finite checker independently evaluates S_r and matches the parametrization in its declared window.

originality.rationale: Subbarao--Yip 1989 contains the order-2 zero-fiber observation for prime p with p+2 composite, but not the exact all-order prime or prime-power fiber formula. Subbarao--Yip 1991 studies general fiber multiplicities without this specialization. The Euler r=1 power-of-two structure is treated as prior, not new. No equivalent indexed statement was located.
residual_risks: L. W. Yip's 1989 doctoral thesis has the same broad inverse-value theme; its full text was not publicly accessible in the inspected routes, so an equivalent formula there cannot be excluded.
The coefficient formula is elementary once the prime-power target is imposed; an unindexed note may have recorded it without appearing in the searched literature.
The fixed-gap corollary is an equivalence and does not prove infinitude of prime pairs.

value.rationale: The archival Schemmel literature explicitly organizes inverse problems by N_r(m), so prime-power fibers are a natural atomic domain. The classification is complete for every r, prime ell and exponent t, not bounded by computation. It sharpens the published order-2 prime obstruction to exact multiplicity, extends the classical Euler 2-power structure, and exposes a direct relation between prime targets and fixed-gap prime pairs.
